statement: An entrepreneur parolee may be considered for one period of re-parole, of up to 30 months, by filing before the initial parole period expires and showing at least a 5 percent ownership interest at adjudication (with at least 5 percent maintained throughout the initial parole), a continued central and active role in an entity that still qualifies as a start-up, and that during the initial parole period the entity received at least $622,142 in qualifying investments or qualified government grants or awards, created at least 5 qualified jobs, or reached at least $622,142 in annual US revenue with average annualized growth of at least 20 percent (partial satisfaction may be supplemented by reliable and compelling evidence of substantial potential for rapid growth and job creation); total entrepreneur parole per start-up entity is capped at 5 years (8 CFR § 212.19(a)(1), (c)(1)-(2), (d)(3), (f), (l)).
caveat: Re-parole, like initial parole, is discretionary case-by-case relief with no appeal and no motion to reopen, and the dollar amounts adjust every 3 years by CPI, so the amounts posted by USCIS at filing time control. This repo does not assess eligibility; immigration decisions need counsel.
